title: Secrets Belong in Files
story:
**From:** Wren Achebe
**Subject:** F-05 -- credential visible to anyone who can run `docker inspect`

Engineer,

I ran `docker inspect uplink` and `docker history kestrel/uplink:1.0`. The satellite uplink's API key appears in plain text in both: it was baked into the image as an `ENV` line. Anyone who pulls this image owns the key.

Rebuild `kestrel/uplink:1.0` without it, and give the container the key as a read-only file at `/run/secrets/api_key`, taken from `/workspace/secrets/api_key.txt`. The program already knows how to read that file.

Rotating the key is Ingrid's job. Yours is making sure it is not in the image.

W.
objectives: Rebuild image `kestrel/uplink:1.0` from `/workspace` without the `API_KEY` environment variable in the image or its history
Replace container `uplink` with one from the new image, publishing host port 8160 to 8000
The container must not receive `API_KEY` as an environment variable
startingState: `kestrel/uplink:1.0` was built with `ENV API_KEY=...` and container `uplink` runs on port 8160. The key file `secrets/api_key.txt` is ready.
hints: Anything in `ENV`, `ARG` or a `RUN` command becomes part of the image's metadata or history, and `docker inspect` shows a container's environment too. Secrets should arrive at runtime, as a file that is not part of the image.

Delete the `ENV API_KEY=...` line from the Dockerfile and rebuild the same tag. Then recreate the container with a bind mount of the key file onto `/run/secrets/api_key`, ending in `:ro`. Do not pass the key with `-e`.

```bash
sed -i '/^ENV API_KEY/d' Dockerfile
docker build -t kestrel/uplink:1.0 .
docker rm -f uplink
docker run -d --name uplink -p 8160:8000 \
  -v /workspace/secrets/api_key.txt:/run/secrets/api_key:ro \
  kestrel/uplink:1.0
```

files.content:
FROM python:3.12-alpine
WORKDIR /srv
ENV API_KEY=kp_live_9Q4xT2
COPY app.py .
CMD ["python", "app.py"]

validation.description: The image's environment no longer contains `API_KEY`
The image history no longer contains the key value
The container has no `API_KEY` environment variable
The key file is bind-mounted read-only at `/run/secrets/api_key`
The uplink authenticates using the mounted key

debrief: Whatever you put in an image layer, `ENV` or `ARG` stays readable by anyone holding the image, so credentials belong in files mounted at runtime (Compose `secrets:` does the same thing). Pro tip: add secret paths to `.dockerignore` so they can never be copied in by accident, and rotate any key that was ever baked into an image.
